explanation: Keep an even-valued prefix followed by odd values already examined. When the next value is even, swap it into the end of the even prefix. Every value is examined once and all original elements remain in the array.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Before each step, the processed prefix consists of evens followed by odds. Swapping a newly found even into the end of the even region extends that region without losing any element. Once every position is examined, all evens precede all odds.
walkthrough: For [3,2,−5,4], move 2 to the front and later move 4 after it. The implementation produces [2,4,−5,3], whose first two values are even and last two odd.
edgeCases: Negative odd numbers must remain in the odd group.
Order within each group is unrestricted.
An empty or already partitioned array remains valid.
